ai.raw_summary: First harmonised standard supporting the AI Act published in the Official Journal Anonymous (not verified) Mon, 10/19/2026 - 09:37 The European Commission has published the reference to the first harmonised standard supporting the implementation of the AI Act in the Official Journal of the European Union. The standard, EN 18286:2026 - Artificial intelligence - Quality management system for EU AI Act regulatory purposes , developed by CEN and CENELEC, provides a clear legal pathway for providers of high-risk AI systems to comply with the quality management system requirements under article 17 of the AI Act . Its publication through Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274 means that providers implementing this standard will benefit from a presumption of conformity with the Article 17 requirements covered by the standard. EN 18286 translates these requirements into an operational quality management system (QMS). It is the only AI QMS standard with a presumption of conformity. It is mapped to Article 17 of the AI Act, built around the AI system lifecycle – rather than the organisation – and designed to be layered on top of the existing international standards – such as ISO/IEC 42001, ISO 9001 or a sectoral QMS (e.g. ISO 13485) – rather than replace them. EN 18286 explicitly allows providers in regulated sectors to integrate management systems, rather than run separate ones. ai.title: SAFETYEDIT: Sparse Internal Targets with Prompt-Wide Control for LLM Jailbreak Backdoors
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.22640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model-editing backdoors aim to induce harmful responses under a trigger while preserving ordinary behavior on untriggered input. Recent model-editing approaches target affirmative response prefixes through rank-one updates to a small subset of model weights. Yet when this prefix-level target is satisfied, the model may still revert to refusal or produce a coherent, apparently compliant response that does not address the request. To overcome this limitation, existing internal-representation approaches shift focus from output tokens to dense, high-dimensional compliance directions in latent space. Existing representation-level approaches rely on preservation constraints to maintain conditionality, motivating us to ask whether a smaller internal target can offer a different effectiveness-preservation trade-off. Motivated by the comparable control capability of single-coordinate interventions, we investigate a sparse refusal-related MLP coordinate as this target. We propose SAFETYEDIT, which optimizes a single refusal-related coordinate and uses KV-cache marking in early attention layers to propagate a prefix-trigger signal across subsequent instruction positions. On some checkpoints a downstream MLP reader converts this signal into control of the coordinate, while on others the propagated signal alone suffices; the method is defined by the sparse target rather than by a fixed writer-reader pair. ai.title: Uncertainty-Aware Budget Allocation for Efficient LLM Tree Search
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.22858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tree search enhances multi-step reasoning in large language models (LLMs), yet prevailing methods expand every step with a fixed budget, irrespective of the marginal utility of expansion. We first show, across existing search algorithms, that continuations sampled from a shared intermediate state are largely duplicates and collapse to a few distinct answers. Critically, we find that the semantic dispersion of sibling actions predicts the redundancy of their downstream continuations, permitting a subtree's budget to be fixed before expansion. An information-theoretic analysis motivates this: treating the per-step budget as the Monte Carlo sample size for estimating a step's residual answer entropy, we derive a sufficient budget that shrinks with sibling dispersion. We accordingly propose $\textbf{Uncertainty-Aware Allocation}$ (UAA), a training-free framework that decouples value from uncertainty: values determine which candidates are promising, while uncertainty, estimated from sibling dispersion at no additional model cost, determines how many merit expansion, via uncertainty-aware pruning and uncertainty-aware budgeting. Across mathematical reasoning, logical reasoning, and planning benchmarks, UAA reduces token usage by up to $90\%$ and latency by up to $9\times$ at comparable accuracy, generalizing across four tree search algorithms and both open- and closed-source LLMs.

ai.title: On the Tip of the Tongue: First-Token Cueing as a Behavioral Probe of Recall Failures in LLMs
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.23400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models often answer factual questions incorrectly in closed-book settings, and such errors are usually attributed to missing knowledge. Yet models often encode answers they fail to produce. We show that many closed-book errors are first-token recall failures: the model commits to a wrong first token, but once given the right one it completes the answer and often recognizes it as correct. We study this with First-Token Cueing, a behavioral probe that prefills the response with the first token of the gold answer. Model uncertainty peaks at the first answer token, where it already predicts correctness, and among gold prefixes of any length the first token alone accounts for the largest share of recovered errors. Across 16 open models, this one token corrects between a fifth and a half of the errors on multi-token answers in English QA and improves accuracy in all seven languages of a multilingual benchmark. Most of the errors it corrects are also solved by the model's own sampled reasoning, a criterion for encoded knowledge, and models recognize correct starts they do not produce: they continue a correct start more confidently than an incorrect start of the same answer type and prior probability, yet rarely find it without the gold answer. These results locate a recoverable class of factual errors at the first decoding step, where inference-time methods may gain the most.
ai.summary: Large language models often answer factual questions incorrectly in closed-book settings, and such errors are usually attributed to missing knowledge.

ai.title: Critical Minerals: BLM Should Ensure Individuals and Businesses Meet Citizenship Requirements for Hardrock Mining Claims
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found The Department of the Interior’s Bureau of Land Management (BLM) administers mining claims that grant the exclusive right to extract critical and other hardrock minerals from most federal lands. U.S. mining laws include citizenship requirements for individuals and business entities holding such claims, known as mining claimants. Under these laws, mining claimants generally must be U.S. citizens, which can include individuals as well as business entities incorporated in a U.S. state or territory. Foreign entities are not qualified to be claimants, but their subsidiaries can hold claims if they are incorporated in the U.S. Mining claimants are not required to disclose to BLM if they are a subsidiary of another entity, foreign or domestic, and they do not have to provide information on any foreign investment they may receive. Under BLM’s regulations and guidance, the agency collects basic identifying information from individuals and business entities holding mining claims. However, BLM generally does not collect citizenship information and does not document if mining claimants meet the U.S. citizenship requirements. In addition, BLM officials said the agency rarely verifies the citizenship of mining claimants. As a result, BLM generally does not know whether mining claimants are qualified to hold mining claims. ai.title: Critical Minerals: Limited Available Information on the Full Extent of Foreign Investment in Mining on Federal Lands
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found The U.S critical mineral supply chain faces numerous constraints, including the need for substantial capital investment and limited domestic processing capacity. The U.S. exports large quantities of domestically extracted ore to Canada, Mexico, and China, among other countries. Copper Mine on Federal Lands The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) and the Forest Service oversee hardrock mines on federal land. As of February 2026, there were 632 approved hardrock mining plans of operation on federal land. The 1872 Mining Law generally requires mining claimants to be U.S. citizens or business entities incorporated in the U.S. Foreign businesses can meet this requirement by having a U.S. subsidiary serve as the claimant. While there is limited available information on the full extent of foreign investment in mining on federal lands and parent-subsidiary relationships, GAO reviewed ownership information of 43 claimants and operators associated with critical mineral mines on federal lands. GAO determined ownership for 32 of those companies and found that 14 were subsidiaries of foreign entities. GAO found that none of the 14 had Chinese-owned parent companies, but in at least two cases, Chinese entities had financial interest in the foreign parent companies. ai.title: Artificial Intelligence: Actions and Opportunities to Implement Responsible Use in DOD
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found Artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in a variety of scenarios, or use cases, in the Department of Defense (DOD). In guidance, DOD established AI Ethical Principles and the concept of Responsible AI to ensure the safety and trustworthiness of AI systems. DOD further defined six tenets to guide Responsible AI implementation. Most of the 10 DOD components GAO surveyed reported taking at least initial steps to establish oversight and implement Responsible AI tenets in the selected surveyed use cases. The Office of the Chief Digital and AI Officer (CDAO), through its Responsible AI Division, established the Responsible AI Working Council as the working-level collaborative group for Responsible AI. However, CDAO officials said the council did not meet from late 2024 until August 2025. Officials from four DOD components told GAO they faced Responsible AI implementation challenges during this time that would have benefited from collaboration. Six of 10 surveyed components reported that sharing Responsible AI resources and best practices would benefit their implementation efforts. Although officials said the council resumed meetings in August 2025, it is at risk of lapsing again as it does not have a charter that defines roles and responsibilities and specifies meeting frequency. trade.raw_summary: 財政部關務署表示，對自中國大陸產製進口特定聚醯胺薄膜課徵反傾銷稅調查案（下稱薄膜反傾銷稅案），財政部及經濟部初步認定有傾銷情事，且對國內產業造成實質損害，為防止我國產業在調查期間繼續遭受損害，財政部公告自115年10月19日起對前述產品臨時課徵反傾銷稅，為期4個月。 關務署說明，薄膜反傾銷稅案傾銷初步調查結果，經財政部關稅稅率審議小組（下稱審議小組）115年9月24日第72次會議審議決議，初步認定除運城集團外，其餘中國大陸涉案廠商均有傾銷事實，相關廠商臨時課徵稅率如下： 特定聚醯胺薄膜反傾銷稅調查案 相關廠商名稱 臨時課徵稅率 運城集團 昆山運城塑業有限公司 運城其龍新材料有限公司 鶴山運城新材料有限公司 0% 其他製造商或出口商 40.21% 關務署進一步說明，依據平衡稅及反傾銷稅課徵實施辦法第14條及第16條規定，財政部應於初步認定公告之翌日起60日內完成有無傾銷之最後認定，經最後認定有傾銷事實者，將移請經濟部於40日內作成傾銷是否損害我國產業之最後調查認定。財政部於接獲經濟部有損害我國產業通知之翌日起10日內提交審議小組審議，審議小組除以傾銷及產業損害等因素為主要之認定基礎，並得斟酌案件對國家整體經濟利益之影響決議是否課徵反傾銷稅。 薄膜反傾銷稅案臨時課徵反傾銷稅公告、傾銷及產業損害初步認定報告，請至關務署官網（https://web.customs.gov.tw/貨物通關/反傾銷及平衡稅措施/調查中案件-反傾銷稅案），及經濟部國際貿易署官網（https://www.trade.gov.tw/經貿往來/我國採行之貿易救濟措施/案件調查/調查中案件）查閱，如有疑問請電洽關務署諮詢專線（02）2550-5500分機1055。 新聞稿聯絡人：王科長 聯絡電話：（02）2550-5500分機1056

trade.raw_summary: 財政部 公告 發文日期：中華民國115年10月13日 發文字號：台財關字第1151027218號 附件： 主旨：力麟科技股份有限公司申請對自中國大陸產製進口特定聚醯胺薄膜課徵反傾銷稅、臨時課徵反傾銷稅及回溯課徵反傾銷稅案，經本部初步認定部分涉案廠商有傾銷情事，自115年10月19日起臨時課徵反傾銷稅。 依據：平衡稅及反傾銷稅課徵實施辦法（下稱實施辦法）第12條至第14條，及本部關稅稅率審議小組115年9月24日第72次會議決議。 公告事項： 一、本部關稅稅率審議小組第72次會議決議略以：本案依據經濟部產業損害初步調查結果，認定有合理跡象顯示，涉案傾銷進口產品對國內產業造成實質損害，且我國產業在調查期間將繼續遭受損害；復經本部初步調查認定部分涉案廠商有傾銷情事，爰依實施辦法第13條規定，對相關涉案廠商之涉案產品臨時課徵反傾銷稅，為期4個月。 二、本案臨時課徵反傾銷稅之範圍、對象、稅率及期間如下： (一)課徵範圍： １、貨品名稱：特定聚醯胺薄膜（Certain Polyamide Film）。 ２、貨品範圍：以重量計含超過50%之聚醯胺-6，不論其表面是否經印刷、塗覆以任何材料或進行任何表面處理，未切或已切成長方形，但未經進一步加工之薄膜或箔。 ３、貨品規格： (１)厚度：0.0114公厘（含）以上至0.0315公厘（含）以下。 (２)寬度：超過5公厘。 (３)排除項目：具下列任一成分或特性之薄膜，不屬涉案貨物： 甲、薄膜表面含有金屬成分者。 乙、攝氏20度至23度且相對溼度50%至65%之測試條件下，薄膜厚度為0.015公厘時，氧氣穿透率小於15mL/(m?·day·atm)，即小於15毫升/(每平方公尺·每日·1標準大氣壓的純氧)者。 ４、參考貨品分類號列：39209229105及39209229203。 ５、用途：應用於食品、化學用品、醫療（藥）用品與電子材料包裝等。 (二)課徵對象： １、輸出國或產製國：中國大陸。 ２、國外製造商及出口商：昆山運城塑業有限公司、運城其龍新材料有限公司、鶴山運城新材料有限公司、廈門長塑實業有限公司、福建長塑實業有限公司、滄州東鴻制膜科技有限公司、滄州東鴻包裝材料有限公司、重慶明珠塑料有限公司、德州東鴻新材料有限公司、蕪湖明珠制膜科技有限公司、曉星化纖（嘉興）有限公司及佛山佛塑科技集團股份有限公司。 ３、國內進口商：慕明企業有限公司、展仝企業有限公司、建?股份有限公司及光展應材股份有限公司。 ４、其他未列名之涉案貨物製造商、出口商或進口商。 (三)臨時課徵稅率： １、昆山運城塑業有限公司（製造商）、運城其龍新材料有限公司（關聯製造商）及鶴山運城新材料有限公司（關聯製造商）：0%。 ２、其他製造商或出口商：40.21%。 ３、前揭個別廠商之臨時課徵稅率，係依其於調查期間提供資料計算決定，故涉案貨物須由該等廠商於該國生產製造並直接出口至我國，始得適用。 (四)課徵期間：依據實施辦法第13條第3項規定，臨時課徵之反傾銷稅，其課徵期間最長為4個月；如經占涉案貿易額相當比例之國外出口商請求，得延長為6個月。 三、本案尚須進行傾銷最後調查，依實地查核結果或其他新事證，可能獲致不同之傾銷差率或作成不同結論。 四、本案後續調查程序：依據實施辦法第14條及第16條規定，本部初步認定之案件，應於初步認定公告之翌日起60日內完成有無傾銷之最後認定。經最後認定有傾銷事實者，本部應即通知經濟部。經濟部應於接獲通知之翌日起40日內，作成該傾銷是否損害我國產業之最後調查認定並通知本部。本部應於接獲經濟部通知之翌日起10日內，提交關稅稅率審議小

trade.source_name: 經濟部國際貿易署 新聞
trade.via: 經濟部國際貿易署 新聞
trade.raw_summary: 為深化臺美經貿合作，經濟部與外貿協會攜手美國在台協會（AIT）及美國州政府辦事處協會（ASOA），於今（13）日在台北國際會議中心舉辦2026年「全球商機鏈結總動員－美國場」（U.S. Business Day），邀請13家美國大型買主來臺，與我國業者進行一對一採購洽談，並由德州、伊利諾州及蒙大拿州等州政府代表介紹當地產業與投資環境，協助臺美企業掌握市場需求、拓展合作機會。 經濟部國際貿易署劉威亷署長於開幕致詞表示，臺灣在半導體、資通訊、機械及電子零組件等領域具有完整的產業聚落與製造能力，美國則擁有廣大市場、人才及多元產業需求，雙方產業優勢高度互補。透過U.S. Business Day，希望讓美國買主更直接認識臺灣優質供應商，也協助臺灣企業更深入了解美國市場需求，進一步促成雙方合作。 貿易署表示，本次來臺買主包括全球首家估值突破10億美元的人形機器人獨角獸Agility Robotics，鎖定智慧工廠及自動化應用尋求臺灣供應鏈夥伴；連續4年來臺參與活動的Telamon Corporation，持續深化5G通訊及工業4.0系統整合採購，為臺美供應鏈合作注入強勁動能。 貿易署指出，近年臺美經貿關係持續深化，2025年美國已躍升為臺灣第一大貿易夥伴，臺灣亦為美國第四大貿易夥伴。隨著雙邊經貿往來日益密切，雙方企業合作領域也持續擴大。經濟部將持續透過商貿交流及企業媒合，鏈結雙方產業優勢與市場需求，為臺美企業創造更多合作契機。 貿易署說明，為協助中小企業拓展國際市場，經濟部後續將於10月19日在臺中國際會展中心舉辦「2026年五金採購洽談會」，邀請全球近50家買主來臺洽談採購，與五金零配件、水五金及手工具等業者進行採購洽談；「2026年高雄國際食品展」亦將於10月22日至25日登場，透過國際買主媒合，協助臺灣業者鏈結國際市場、拓展全球商機。 貿易署發言人：胡副署長 聯絡電話：02-2397-7109、02-2397-7178、0966-525-106 業務聯絡人：雙邊貿易二組謝組長 聯絡電話：(02)2397-7401

trade.title: Critical Minerals: Limited Available Information on the Full Extent of Foreign Investment in Mining on Federal Lands
trade.raw_summary: What GAO Found The U.S critical mineral supply chain faces numerous constraints, including the need for substantial capital investment and limited domestic processing capacity. The U.S. exports large quantities of domestically extracted ore to Canada, Mexico, and China, among other countries. Copper Mine on Federal Lands The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) and the Forest Service oversee hardrock mines on federal land. As of February 2026, there were 632 approved hardrock mining plans of operation on federal land. The 1872 Mining Law generally requires mining claimants to be U.S. citizens or business entities incorporated in the U.S. Foreign businesses can meet this requirement by having a U.S. subsidiary serve as the claimant. While there is limited available information on the full extent of foreign investment in mining on federal lands and parent-subsidiary relationships, GAO reviewed ownership information of 43 claimants and operators associated with critical mineral mines on federal lands. GAO determined ownership for 32 of those companies and found that 14 were subsidiaries of foreign entities. GAO found that none of the 14 had Chinese-owned parent companies, but in at least two cases, Chinese entities had financial interest in the foreign parent companies.
